messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: multi-GPU collective silent freeze detected in cluster-gamma. Affected tenants: 2 Dedicated prod tenants running TP4 pipeline-parallel inference. Auto-escalating to oncall. Pager: HIGH.

monica: oncall here, looking. which hosts? any immediate customer errors?

incidents-bot: impacted hosts: gpu-node-115, gpu-node-116, gpu-node-117. Symptoms: processes in RUNNING state with no token output ~65s. NCCL logs: repeated allreduce handshake stalls. No explicit OOM in dmesg, but elevated inference error rates observed.

rick-eng-runtime: grabbing perf traces. KV cache builds fine then everything stops. dmesg shows nvpeer errors around the freeze. log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] NCCL WARN Call to ncclCommInitRank timed out, retrying
[2026-03-15T10:12:04Z] ncclAllReduce timeout waiting for peer 3
[2026-03-15T10:12:05Z] CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at /build/.../kernel.cu:432
[2026-03-15T10:12:05Z] process 23456 pinned to gpu:3 caught signal 7
```

priya-sre: CUDA ILLEGAL_ADDRESS + comm init timeouts = either bad kernel memory access or driver/runtime mismatch. Any recent driver or kernel updates on that node pool?

carla-ml: we shipped a fused-quant patch last night that affects rotary/fused matmul kernels. The affected tenants are opt-in to the new quant profile. Could be correlated.

monica: plan: 1) isolate the three nodes (cordon+drain), 2) snapshot logs + core dumps, 3) restart runtime on nodes, 4) if not recovered, failover affected tenants to single-GPU fallback model, 5) CS to notify. Who can run drains?

priya-sre: I can. doing now:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-115
kubectl drain gpu-node-115 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force --timeout=5m
```

rick-eng-runtime: wait on evictions until we snapshot /var/log/nvidia and any core dumps. we lose ephemeral traces on restart. pulling bundles to /tmp/incident-3965432100/

priya-sre: logs saved: /tmp/incident-3965432100/node-115.tgz, perms set for eng. proceeding with drain now.

carla-ml: pushing the diff for the fused-quant change to this thread. if memory layout assumptions changed, it could trigger illegal address on certain TP ranks.

ryan-cs: pinging tenants now with an interim message: \"We092re investigating a transient tensor-parallel slowdown impacting inference throughput. We092ve isolated hosts and are pursuing mitigation; update in 30m.\" Send?

monica: yes send. don't speculate on cause. include support contact.

ryan-cs: message sent. tenant A asked for immediate retry/fallback.

rick-eng-runtime: after snapshots I restarted redwood-runtime on node-115:
```
systemctl restart redwood-runtime
journalctl -u redwood-runtime -n 200 --no-pager | grep -i nccl
```
runtime came up but nvpeer warnings persist; some worker pids still hanging in kernel space. tracebacks reference symbols in libredwood_quant.so (fused ops).

carla-ml: can we toggle off quant for a single job to validate? we have per-job env: REDWOOD_FORCE_QUANT=0.

monica: try it on one affected job (tenant A) and see if tokens resume.

rick-eng-runtime: toggled env + restarted worker for tenant A. worker restarted and token streaming resumed immediately. that isolates to quant fused kernel.

carla-ml: confirmed. looks like memory-safety bug in fused-quant under TP4 rank layout. prepare rollback of fused op from production artifact registry.

priya-sre: cordoning+draining node-116 and node-117 now. evictions completed; no new cores during migration. scheduling rollback across runtime fleet.

monica: enable routing fallback for in-flight customers while we repair. example API call we used:
```
POST /v1/routing/override
{ "route": "tenant-A", "fallback_model": "tp4-single-gpu-v1", "duration": "30m" }
```

ryan-cs: tenants notified that quant kernels are disabled and fallback applied. tenant A requested an RCA and a rough ETA; giving 2-3h.

incidents-bot: alert suppression enabled for the duration to reduce noise.

carla-ml: opening a high-priority PR to revert the fused-quant commit and add a safety check for TP rank memory bounds. also adding targeted unit/regression tests for TP4 shapes.

rick-eng-runtime: will gate fused op behind feature flag OFF by default for dedicated/prod pools. will roll runtime change to canary first.

priya-sre: rolling canary to 10% non-prod; holding prod until PR merges and we validate.

monica: runbook summary to include in pager followup: cause hypothesis 096 memory corruption in fused quant kernel under TP layout provoking NCCL allreduce stalls and CUDA ILLEGAL_ADDRESS; mitigations 096 disabled quant per-job, cordoned/drained and restarted nodes, rolled back fused kernel and gated feature. customer comms: interim notice sent, failover route applied, RCA promised.

ryan-cs: will coordinate postmortem doc with engs; customer A expects short writeup.

carla-ml: scheduling a 24h synthetic stress job with TP4 shapes to validate rollback & tests.

monica: final ops checklist: - affected nodes cordoned: YES; - logs snapped/backed up: YES; - runtime restarted and nodes reprovisioned: YES; - failing jobs recovered via disable-quant or fallback: YES; - customers notified and fallback applied: YES.

priya-sre: monitoring shows normalized token throughput across clusters. keeping watch for 60m then will uncordon hosts if stable.

monica: closing live incident. reopen if new signals. filing pager followups for full RCA. :white_check_mark:

incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED 096 mitigated. last update: 3965432399
